label: Dynamics of Open Chains
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 271 through 324 and asks how forces, torques, velocities, and accelerations interact through a manipulator's configuration. We add a configuration-dependent metric to kinematics, then build two efficient recursive passes along the chain that turn that geometry into computable torques and accelerations.

label: Inverse vs Forward Dynamics
notes: Open-chain dynamics answers two complementary queries built from the same ingredients. Inverse dynamics is given the motion and returns the torques that produce it, while forward dynamics is given the torques and predicts acceleration. Inverse drives control and trajectory tracking; forward drives simulation, and each reuses the same mass, velocity, and gravity terms.

label: The Manipulator Equation
notes: The manipulator equation collects every effect into three labelled terms. The mass matrix multiplies acceleration, the velocity-product vector gathers Coriolis and centripetal coupling, and the gravity vector loads the joints at rest. Reading torque as the sum of these parts makes the structure of robot dynamics inspectable rather than a wall of symbols.

label: Mass Matrix as a Metric
notes: Kinetic energy is a quadratic form in joint velocity, and the symmetric positive-definite mass matrix is its metric. Its smallest eigenvalue measuring how cheaply the lightest motion direction accelerates must stay positive, confirming energy never collapses along any joint-velocity direction. The matrix changes as links fold because masses move nearer or farther from joints.

label: Christoffel Symbols and Coriolis
notes: The velocity-product term is not arbitrary; its coefficients are the Christoffel symbols of the mass matrix, built from partial derivatives of its entries. This ties Coriolis and centripetal forces directly to how inertia varies with configuration. When the mass matrix is constant the symbols vanish and these velocity-coupling forces disappear entirely from the equation.

label: Spatial Inertia and Twists
notes: The recursive formulation lives in SE(3) using twists and wrenches. Each link carries a six-by-six spatial inertia matrix combining rotational inertia and mass. A twist packages angular and linear velocity into one screw, and the spatial momentum is the spatial inertia applied to that twist, giving a single covariant momentum object per link.

label: Newton-Euler: Forward Pass
notes: The forward pass propagates motion outward from the base to the tip. Starting from the fixed base twist and acceleration, each joint adds its own contribution, and the adjoint map transports the parent twist into the child frame. By the end every link knows its twist and acceleration, ready for the force computation that follows.

label: Newton-Euler: Backward Pass
notes: The backward pass propagates wrenches inward from the tip to the base. At each link Newton-Euler equates the net wrench to spatial inertia times acceleration plus a velocity-product term, and adds the wrench transmitted from the child. Projecting each joint wrench onto its screw axis yields exactly the joint torque sought.

label: Power Pairing Invariant
notes: Torques do work through joint rates and spatial wrenches do work through twists, and a correct frame transform must preserve that scalar power. The adjoint maps the twist while its inverse transpose maps the wrench, so their pairing is unchanged. Checking this invariant catches inverse-dynamics code that assigns torque to the wrong frame.

label: Forward Dynamics by Inversion
notes: Forward dynamics inverts the manipulator equation. Run inverse dynamics with zero acceleration to obtain the bias forces, subtract them from applied torque, then solve the mass-matrix linear system for acceleration. The composite rigid-body and articulated-body algorithms compute the mass matrix and its inverse action efficiently using the same recursive chain structure.

label: Task-Space Inertia
notes: Mapping dynamics through the Jacobian gives the operational-space formulation, where the task-space inertia is the Jacobian-inverse-transpose times mass times Jacobian-inverse. Near singularities the Jacobian loses directions and this inertia becomes ill-conditioned, so manipulability warns when the apparent endpoint mass blows up along lost directions of motion.

label: Actuators and Gearing
notes: Real joints carry motor inertia and gearing that reshape apparent dynamics. A gear ratio scales reflected rotor inertia by its square, so high ratios make the actuator dominate the link inertia. Ignoring this term makes aggressive motions look unrealistically cheap, hiding the true torque and energy cost of fast acceleration.

label: Recap and Takeaways
notes: Two ideas carry the chapter. Dynamics adds a configuration-dependent metric, the mass matrix, on top of kinematics, and the efficient algorithms are simply structured passes through the chain. Inverse and forward dynamics share ingredients, Newton-Euler recursion computes them in linear time, and coordinate choice changes appearance but never the underlying physics.
